newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - March 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - March 6.

text.p: PRAVO - The Senate approved the Czech-German Declaration on Wednesday evening without any additional proclamation emphasising an end to past problems and closing property questions.

- Pro Win, which became the majority shareholder of Poldi Steel after buying Bohemia Art from Marko Stehlik, has decided not to hold on to Poldi for long, but to profit in mediating its sale, a spokesman for the FNM, Milos Ruzicka, said after the first meeting between the National Property Fund (FNM) and Pro Win yesterday.
LIDOVE NOVINY - The general director of Czech Railways, Rudolf Mladek, sent a letter to the cabinet announcing his intention to resign from his position when he returns from his holiday.
- Spent nuclear waste will be stored in the Czech Republic in structures in both of the Czech Republic's nuclear power plants, Temelin and Dukovany. The cabinet decided on this yesterday.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - According to Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy, more companies will be allowed to enter the tender for Aero Vodochody. Dlouhy is presenting a new deadline for applications, which prolongs the tender for four weeks.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik's administration already has material for budget cuts prepared, due to the 6.7 billion crown deficit in the government budget at the end of February.
- Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka announced net profits for 1996 of 3.09 billion crowns.
- The cabinet approved a plan for a law about foreign residence in the Czech Republic and for a law about asylum, according to Interior Minister Jan Ruml.
- By the end of last November, domestic banks wrote off more than 20 billion crowns for bad loans, which is 18 billion more than in November of 1995.
- Tenants believe that the government coalition's plans to deregulate rents by the year 2000 are unacceptable for most residents.
